reading: The proposal (E9), not applied, rewords only q-right-revocable (E1): the training condition, already one clause of the baseline question (E5), becomes its hinge and is tied in time to the finale choice ('before the finale mechanism is chosen'). Revocability and who carries the Turn when the lineages end stay in the wording. Every listed mechanism is preserved unchanged; the change is one of emphasis and sequencing in one question. Interpretation: by asking about training before the finale, the question now leans on the Long Return's timetable (E82) and on the crews' leverage in Books 27-29 (E2). Book 24 already records a decision on this question (E8) and an inherited training condition with a review point (E84); whether Book 24 carries the new hinge is not established.

concerns.title: Training condition becomes the hinge of the Special Draw Right
concerns.earlier: Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent, what training condition does it carry, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
concerns.proposed: Is the training condition the hinge of the lineage Special Draw Right: are apprentices from outside the lineage trained under the Right before the finale mechanism is chosen? Is the Right revocable or permanent, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
concerns.reading: The instruction (E1) names this change. In the baseline (E5, E7) the training condition is one of three co-equal sub-questions and is asked as 'what condition'. The proposal (E9) asks whether a specific condition, training outside apprentices, is actually met, and makes it the question's lead. Interpretation: the question moves from the design of the Right to whether its condition is performed in story time. A changed wording does not prove the author's meaning changed beyond that.
counterevidence: The lineage node already records the Right as conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage (E33), so the hinge may only make explicit what was recorded.
concerns.competing_reading: The rewording may be purely clarifying: the condition was already the operative part of the Right, and the proposal only orders the clauses to match.

concerns.title: Revocability and the end of the lineages stay in the question
concerns.earlier: Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent ... and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end?
concerns.proposed: Is the Right revocable or permanent, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
concerns.reading: Both remaining clauses of the baseline wording (E5) appear in the proposed wording (E9), and the question keeps its identity, as the instruction requires (E1). The question is still recorded as not decided. What these clauses mean once they follow the training hinge is an interpretation.

concerns.title: The question is newly sequenced against the finale choice
concerns.proposed: ... are apprentices from outside the lineage trained under the Right before the finale mechanism is chosen?
concerns.reading: The proposed wording (E9) introduces a temporal relation to q-finale-mechanism, whose wording is unchanged (E10, E14). The baseline wording had no such ordering. Interpretation: the discovery origin (E3) observed that the finale choice may answer parts of q-right-revocable; the new clause instead asks whether training is settled, or at least under way, before that choice, which makes the training a precondition the finale inherits rather than a consequence of it.
counterevidence: The packet does not record when the finale mechanism is chosen in story time; Books 27-29 carry ratification only under Alternative C (E24).
concerns.competing_reading: The clause may mark a planning order for the author (decide training before deciding the finale) rather than an order of events in the story.

concerns.title: Revocability may lose its place as the question's first concern
concerns.earlier: Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent ...
concerns.proposed: Revocability is asked second, after the training hinge.
concerns.reading: The baseline opens with revocability (E5), and Book 24's decision records the question as 'whether the Right is revocable or permanent, and the training condition it carries' (E8). The proposal moves revocability behind the hinge (E9). Interpretation: if the hinge governs, revocability may become a consequence of whether training happens rather than a question of its own. The instruction names the hinge, not a demotion of revocability, so the intent of any displacement is not established.
counterevidence: The instruction says to change nothing else (E1), and the proposed wording still asks revocability in full (E9).
concerns.competing_reading: Ordering is not ranking: revocability may remain an equal concern that simply follows the hinge in the sentence.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved. The node records the Right as conditional on training outside apprentices and, in working design, revocable by the Council. Interpretation: the proposal draws on this recorded condition rather than adding one; the node is unchanged, but the question now asks whether its condition is met.
mechanisms.conditional_consequence: If the hinge is adopted and outside apprentices are not trained before the finale, the recorded condition would stand unmet when A, B or C is chosen; what follows for the Right is not recorded.

counterevidence.text: Book 24 already carries this condition with a review point in that Book (E84), so the hinge may change little in the Books already proposed.

unresolved: Whether the Council's revocation power depends on the training condition is not recorded.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved. The link gives skill a claim on draw. Interpretation: with training as the hinge, the claim's justification may shift from holding skill to transferring it, but the recorded function is unchanged.
mechanisms.conditional_consequence: Under Alternative A, which decouples draw from hands (E50), a claim expressed as draw may have nothing to attach to (E3); the training hinge could then be the part of the Right that survives.

counterevidence.text: The discovery origin reads the finale choice, not the training condition, as what may revoke or transform the Right (E3).

unresolved: Whether the Right survives Alternative A in any form is not recorded.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved. Keeping the channels records that lineage crews carry repair from Book 20 and that households able to meet the rota carry the rest. Interpretation: outside apprentices are the recorded route by which this labour could stop depending on the lineages, which is what the question's last clause asks about.
mechanisms.conditional_consequence: If outside apprentices are trained before the finale, the answer to who carries the Turn when the lineages end may be partly given before Book 30; this is interpretation.

counterevidence.text: Book 24 inherits that a generation after Book 20 has never seen the labour because crews perform it under the Right (E86), which may make outside training harder to stage early.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved. The Long Return needs channel labour before its date (E67). Interpretation: asking whether apprentices are trained before the finale ties the training question to the pulse's timetable, which Book 24 records as public, with training taking years (E82).
mechanisms.conditional_consequence: If the hinge is adopted, the date may function as a clock on the training condition; the packet records no such clock.

counterevidence.text: Book 24 records that it does not depend on the Hollow Gate (E102); the pulse's routing need not bear on training at all.

unresolved: Whether the Long Return's labour must come from trained crews or from any hands is not recorded.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved. Hands and draw is the governing variable and each finale mechanism answers it differently. Interpretation: the reworded question does not touch this thread directly; it bears on it only through the Right's claim on draw and the finale ordering.

counterevidence.text: The Book 20 conversion's blind spot (E94) shows the governing variable can be pressed without reference to training.

inheritance.text: Book 24's inherited element records the Right as conditional on training outside apprentices, with its review point in Book 24. It cites the lineage node. This inheritance exists in the baseline; it is not created by the proposal.
Book 25 carries the same inherited training condition, citing the lineage node; its decisions are not examined (E26).

Book 24's decision cites q-right-revocable on its current wording and reaches the review point. Whether Book 24 would carry the training hinge if the author adopts the rewording is an interpretation; the decision is recorded against the baseline wording.

Book 24 inherits that the Long Return's date is public and that training takes years, so the labour question cannot wait for Books 27 onward. This is the recorded element through which a 'before the finale' hinge could reach Book 24.
Book 24 inherits that a generation after Book 20 has never seen the labour, because crews perform it under the Right; this is the cohort from which outside apprentices would come.
Book 25 is recorded only by its title here, and its decisions are not examined; the records do not establish whether it carries this question in either wording.

trajectories.title: Training as the clock before the finale

steps.text: The Right is recorded as conditional on training outside apprentices; the proposal would make that condition the question's hinge.
Book 24 records the Long Return's date as public and training as taking years.
Book 24's review point of the Right could become the moment the valley sees whether outside apprentices are actually being trained.
Hypothetical: by Books 27-29 the crews argue for B or a low C threshold, and their leverage depends on whether trained outsiders already exist.

assumptions: Training is understood as a story-time process, not only a planning order.

comparison.creative_gain: Gives the crews' finale choice a prior, visible cost and makes the Right's condition dramatisable before Book 30.
comparison.narrative_cost: Commits Books 24-29 to stage training progress, which may crowd other concerns.
comparison.contrivance_risk: A clean deadline could feel engineered if the date and training span are made to fit too neatly.
comparison.future_commitment: Fixes an order: training is settled or failing before A, B or C is chosen.
comparison.flexibility: Leaves revocability and the finale mechanism open.

trajectories.title: Uncounted training under the gift reading

steps.text: The proposal asks whether apprentices are trained under the Right.
In Book 24 the cohort refuses to be entered in the stewardship tally when the Council asks for recorded apprentices.
Interpretation: training may happen without being recorded, so whether the condition is met becomes a question of what counts as training under the Right.
Hypothetical: the finale inherits a Right whose condition is met in practice but not in the record, pressing A against B.

assumptions: The cohort's refusal to be tallied extends to apprenticeship.
The Council is the body that judges the condition.

comparison.creative_gain: Joins the training hinge to the series' question of whether giving must be counted.
comparison.narrative_cost: Makes the condition ambiguous at the point the proposal wants it decisive.
comparison.contrivance_risk: Low if the refusal is given its own reasons, as Book 24 proposes.
comparison.future_commitment: Ties the Right to the tally's standing.
comparison.flexibility: Keeps the condition answerable either way.

alternatives.title: Adopt the training hinge as worded
alternatives.summary: Accept the reworded q-right-revocable: training outside apprentices before the finale becomes the hinge, with revocability and the end of the lineages following. Any loss of revocability's lead place is accepted, not resolved.
alternatives.gains: Makes the recorded condition of the Right a question that Books 24-29 can stage, and gives the crews' finale choice a prior stake.
alternatives.costs: Sequences the question against the finale, which commits later Books to show training, and may subordinate revocability.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether Book 24's decision (E8) and its review point (E84) read naturally against the new wording.

alternatives.title: Keep the three co-equal sub-questions
alternatives.summary: Keep the baseline wording, in which revocability, the training condition and the end of the lineages are asked together without an order against the finale.
alternatives.gains: Leaves Book 24's recorded decision exactly aligned with its question and avoids committing a timetable.
alternatives.costs: The training condition stays one clause among three and the crews' finale leverage gains no prior stake.
alternatives.next_investigation: Ask whether the finale choice alone, as the discovery origin suggests (E3), is meant to answer the Right.

alternatives.title: Split the training hinge from revocability
alternatives.summary: Keep q-right-revocable for revocability and the end of the lineages, and develop a distinct new question, not given an identity here, asking whether outside apprentices are trained before the finale. Each can then be answered in its own Book.
alternatives.gains: Lets the training timetable be settled in Book 24 without deciding whether the Right is revocable.
alternatives.costs: Adds a question, which the instruction (E1) does not ask for, and may split a concern the Right holds together.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether the Council's revocation power is meant to depend on the training condition (E33).

alternatives.title: Defer until Book 24's review point is drafted
alternatives.summary: Keep the question and the lineage node as recorded, and reconsider the hinge once Book 24's review point of the Right is written; that Book, which inherits the condition and the public date, would show whether the hinge is needed.
alternatives.gains: Lets Book 24's own development decide whether training is the operative part of the Right.
alternatives.costs: Leaves the ordering against the finale unstated while Books 24-26 are drafted.
alternatives.next_investigation: Draft Book 24's review point (E84) and see whether training or revocability carries the scene.
